record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.context_brief: Polynomial density in weighted Bergman spaces
record.original_question: Let omega be a continuous function on the unit disk D satisfying (1 - |z|^2)^2 ≤ omega(z) ≤ 2(1 - |z|^2). In the weighted Bergman space L2_a(D, omega) of holomorphic functions f with integral_D |f(z)|^2 omega(z) dS(z) finite, must the polynomials be dense? If this is not known under only those bounds, does polynomial density follow after adding the regularity condition Delta^2 omega ≥ 4 on D?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. Suppose omega is a continuous function on D satisfying (1 - |z|2)2 ≤ omega(z) ≤ 2(1 - |z|2), z ∈ D.

Must then the polynomials be dense in the weighted Bergman space L2_a(D, omega) of all holomorphic functions in D having integral_D |f(z)|2 omega(z) dS(z) < +∞? What if we make the regularity assumption on omega that Delta2 omega ≥ 4 on D?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk, and let $dS$ denote area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. Suppose $\omega:\mathbb{D}\to(0,\infty)$ is a continuous function satisfying
$$(1-|z|^2)^2 \le \omega(z) \le 2(1-|z|^2), \qquad z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
Define the weighted Bergman space
$$L^2_a(\mathbb{D},\omega) \;=\; \Big\{f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C} \text{ holomorphic} : \|f\|_\omega^2 := \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\,\omega(z)\,dS(z) < +\infty\Big\}.$$
Question (a): Must the set of holomorphic polynomials be dense in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D},\omega)$?
Question (b): If density is not known under the hypotheses above alone, does it follow if one additionally assumes the regularity condition
$$\Delta^2\omega(z) \;\ge\; 4 \qquad \text{for all } z\in\mathbb{D},$$
where $\Delta$ is the standard Laplacian (so $\omega$ is in particular superbiharmonic)?
artifact.status_search_result: The regularity-assumption variant appears to be resolved: it is known that polynomials are dense in weighted Bergman spaces on the disk whose weights are superbiharmonic and satisfy a boundary growth bound of the form $0\le\omega(z)\le C(1-|z|)$ (a setting that covers the case $\Delta^2\omega\ge 4$ together with $\omega\le 2(1-|z|^2)$). The general question without the superbiharmonicity-type regularity assumption does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Norm Approximation by Polynomials in Some Weighted Bergman Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomials are dense in weighted Bergman spaces on the unit disk whose weights are superbiharmonic and vanish in an average sense at the boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Density of polynomials is established for superbiharmonic weights with appropriate boundary decay, covering the regularity-assumption case.

status_evidence.title: Density of polynomials in certain weighted Dirichlet type spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Analytic polynomials are dense in weighted Dirichlet type spaces if the weight function is super-biharmonic and satisfies a growth condition up to the boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Related density results rely on the super-biharmonic hypothesis plus a boundary growth condition.
